acceptance: 1) Caller/wiring point: real ADMIN handler -> recovery-authorizations. Current password plus a new TOTP obtains RECOVERY_AUTHORIZE bound to another target before a 15-minute permit is issued. The target cannot be self. Old bodyless direct reset, session-only requests, visitor email requests, SALES, and EDITOR all reject without changing target factors (E-13). 2) The permit is a random 256-bit value, stored only as a hash and returned once. Grant consumption and target/source/reason audit commit together. Reusing a grant issues no second permit; logs contain no plaintext permit, and response loss does not automatically issue another. An ordinary passwordless session cannot use this path to omit the current password (E-73, E-75).

E-13.scene: C-04 Lost authenticator and single-administrator recovery
E-13.trigger: Another administrator authorizes recovery on someone else's behalf.
E-13.expect: The authorizer must authenticate again. An already open admin page or a visitor email request alone cannot authorize resetting another account.

E-73.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-73.trigger: Two requests use the same ActionGrant concurrently, or a password-change grant is used to disable the authenticator.
E-73.expect: Within the sensitive-change transaction, validate and consume the grant once against the action, device, account, and credential version. Only one matching request succeeds; reject a mismatched purpose without executing the change.

E-75.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-75.trigger: The user forgets the current password but can still use previously enabled passwordless sign-in.
E-75.expect: Resolve D3 through the restricted recovery path and one-time permit/restricted cookie already defined in sections 09/10. Ordinary passwordless sign-in remains unchanged. Without the current password, sensitive settings cannot issue an ordinary ActionGrant: reject direct requests based solely on a signed-in session or one TOTP without a change. Restricted recovery permits only new enrollment and is audited.
